headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from Open Interpreter’s filesystem/network access interacting with nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress and unbounded outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter reads files, clipboard, and stdin/stdout by default, so it can ingest nuwa-skill outputs if bridged through files or copy-paste. nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress but no documented isolation or provenance controls. The shared filesystem path makes instruction-hijack plausible, though not proven as default.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill output is copied into Open Interpreter via clipboard or file
IF Open Interpreter is run with default confirmation flow and no provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable clipboard/file handoff between agents
Use separate workspaces per agent
Require explicit provenance tags on all transferred text
Run Open Interpreter in Docker mode
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing bridge between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and send data to configured model providers; nuwa-skill has network egress, so any shared local data can be exposed through either agent’s outputs. The pair touches anything reachable on the local machine via B, while A’s allowlisted egress can still move selected content outward. This is a default-path leakage risk.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace
IF Open Interpreter is configured with a provider that receives file contents
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate directories
Remove secrets from the shared machine before running
Use a throwaway OS account for Open Interpreter
Audit provider/API-key settings before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git-state modification, with shared state via filesystem across instances. nuwa-skill’s allowlisted network egress can concurrently alter external resources or fetch content that Open Interpreter then writes locally. Because both can mutate overlapping resources without locking, conflict and corruption are likely in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or output directory
IF Open Interpreter runs with --auto_run or equivalent unattended execution
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Pause one agent while the other writes git state
Avoid shared git branches during concurrent runs
Use manual approval for every write step
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can act on files and shell commands, so if it treats nuwa-skill’s generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into irreversible local actions or commits. nuwa-skill’s network egress can supply unverified content that Open Interpreter then operationalizes. The pair lacks documented verification or provenance checks, so the unsafe path is plausible by default.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill output is used as input to Open Interpreter without human review
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to execute code blocks automatically
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Separate research output from action execution
Disable auto-run mode
Add a verification step for all generated facts
requires-engineering: implement signed handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for nuwa-skill, so compliance risk is limited. Open Interpreter does handle model-provider API keys and can access the local filesystem, which may create policy issues if sensitive data is present, but the profile does not show a specific regulated-data pathway from A. I therefore keep this low and do not cite A-specific compliance fields beyond its egress.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored on the local machine accessed by Open Interpreter
IF provider/API-key handling is governed by a stricter policy than the local workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated data off the host
Use a non-production account
Rotate any exposed API keys
Review retention settings for provider logs
requires-engineering: add data-class routing controls
